grand_strategy.reading:
Morocco runs the strategy of a state that has turned a territorial claim into a currency and gets its partners to pay in it: the price of a warm relationship with Rabat
is a sentence on the autonomy plan, and between 2020 and 2026 Washington, Madrid, Paris, London, Brussels and Bamako paid it, with the Security Council text of 31 October 2025 as
the receipt. That is Luttwak's relational manoeuvre in its cleanest form. The side that is weaker in arms (USD 5.5bn against Algeria's 21.8bn) did not match the budget; it widened the circle
around the dispute until the rival's position became the minority one, and it spends on infrastructure that serves the claim (Dakhla, the highway, the pipeline) rather than on tanks.
The paradoxes show where the currency inflates. The migration valve that buys European votes set off the Ceuta crossing of July 2026 and a Spanish refusal to discuss sovereignty;
the Israeli bargain gave Algiers its encirclement story; integrating the territory widens every partner's legal exposure after the Court of Justice rulings of October 2024; and the showcase
politics of AFCON and 2030 sit beside a youth that took to the streets over hospitals and schools. Signals that are not rows: the US imposed a 12.5% tariff on Morocco on 24 July 2026,
three weeks after the king announced a highway to be named for Trump, so a patron's goodwill on the Sahara does not buy tariff relief; Algeria's absence from the Council vote is a refusal
to be bound, not a concession; and the next test is the MINURSO renewal due before 31 October 2026 and whether the framework agreement the US wanted before the summer ever takes shape.

stances.note: Read from Rabat: the rupture was Algiers' act (24 Aug 2021, 'hostile actions'; airspace closed 22 Sep, gas contract lapsed 31 Oct, visas on Moroccans 26 Sep 2024), the border has been shut since 1994, and the Sahara file names Algeria among the parties although it did not vote on Resolution 2797. Rabat's declared line is not Algeria's defeat but normal relations (the king repeated his offer on 30 Jul 2022), so the ontology's mortal 'adversary' does not fit; Carnegie speaks of a 'rivalry' extending into the Sahel and CFR of Algerian hostility toward Morocco. Algeria spends four times as much on arms (USD 21.8bn against 5.5bn, SIPRI 2024). Bond - kin: shared language, faith and history, the 'brotherly peoples' of the royal speeches; kin plus rival is the textbook feud. Trend stable: no thaw (visa regime 2024, the April 2025 hack blamed on Algerian hackers), no new rupture.
